_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey and the `for k, v := range report` info-key skip natively (doctor_verdict.go no longer declares them); the placeholder refusal, the no-credential row and doctorUnexpectedStatus are still connector-only and re-applied by hand.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install) ZAMMAD_BASE_URL stays an empty string in the install blocks (a filled placeholder would override ZAMMAD_URL, config.go instanceBaseURLOverride), and the HTTP-mode text does not claim a 404 at the root (StreamableHTTPServer answers every path).
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For zammad the manifest gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. server.json gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now also reads ZAMMAD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (bearer token for --transport http) and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE (tenant-gated client profile binding); both are declared on all three channels the way datagate declares them, and check_env_schema.py is what noticed. The 4.32 press reads ZAMMAD_USER_AGENT through cliutil.EnvOverride (client.go, deliver.go); once check_env_schema.py learned to follow that cross-package helper (#339) it became a visible read, so it is declared optional on all three channels the way auvik/avanan/threatlocker declare <SLUG>_USER_AGENT. The remote launch line in mcp-install.md (and the README / page.json ChatGPT answer) dropped the `--addr :7777` that onboard emits: the 4.32.5 server refuses a non-loopback --addr without --tls-cert/--tls-key (verified: "non-loopback --addr \":7777\" requires --tls-cert and --tls-key"), and its loopback default is already 127.0.0.1:7777; the line also gained ZAMMAD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, without which --transport http refuses to start.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

handfixes.summary: hand-authored novel_wiring.go registers, through wireHandBuiltCommands, called from root.go (not the generator's registerNovelCommand hook from init, since nothing able to reach output may run before credkit.Start), the commands the generator does not wire: `articles sync` under `articles`, and the carried stale/orphans/load workflow commands at the root
handfixes.why: Since press 4.32.5 the generator wires the research.json novels itself (root-level ones in root.go, kb browse/get/search in kb.go via addNovelCommandIfAbsent), but `articles sync` is a hand-authored command that is not a research.json novel, and stale/orphans/load are carried workflow commands the 4.32.5 press no longer emits, so nothing generated registers any of the four - they compiled, the tests passed, and the CLI and MCP server simply did not have them. root.go's registerNovelCommand hook is the press's sanctioned extension point (hooks run after every generated parent is attached, from init, without editing root.go), so the wiring survives a force regeneration by construction instead of as a BODY-DRIFT edit to articles.go. A fresh-base reprint that forgets to carry this file drops four shipped commands and four MCP tools while everything stays green; these asserts are what notices.

handfixes.summary: `stale`, `orphans` and `load` (pm_stale.go / pm_orphans.go / pm_load.go) are carried as hand files: press 4.28.0 emitted them as project-management workflow templates, the 4.32.5 profiler classes Zammad as the 'content' archetype and no longer emits them
handfixes.why: The three commands (and their MCP tools of the same names, all mcp:read-only) shipped in every zammad release through v0.1.5. cli-printing-press selects the pm_* workflow templates only when the profiler's VisionaryPlan archetype is 'project-management'; 4.32.5 classifies this spec as 'content' (visible in `context` output), so a plain regeneration silently removes three shipped commands while build, vet, test and every docs gate stay green (no README/SKILL/guide line names them). They compile unchanged against the 4.32.5 store API; their generated header was replaced by a hand-carried note and they are wired by novel_wiring.go. Retire this entry only when the shipped surface is intentionally trimmed and the CHANGELOG says so.

handfixes.summary: config.Load honours ZAMMAD_URL (instance root, /api/v1 appended) and ZAMMAD_BASE_URL (explicit API base, wins) through os.Getenv literals, so the CLI can be pointed at the operator's instance at all
handfixes.why: The shipped base_url is a placeholder (https://your-instance.zammad.com/api/v1) and every install surface - README, SKILL, guide, the .mcpb prompt, server.json and mcp-install.md - tells the operator to set ZAMMAD_URL. The 4.28.0 tree carried a hand-wired ZAMMAD_URL block in config.go that was never recorded in this ledger; the 4.32.5 regeneration dropped it, leaving a CLI that reads only ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, and only check_env_schema.py ('ZAMMAD_URL is declared in manifest.json but NO source file reads it') noticed - build, vet, test and every docs gate stayed green while the documented way to reach a real instance was gone. Both reads go through os.Getenv literals (the generated read used cliutil.EnvOverride, which the env-schema scanner cannot resolve) with cliutil.EffectiveEnv keeping the generator's unresolved-${user_config} placeholder handling. config_instance_url_test.go pins the resolution order in behaviour, not just in strings.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press could model an instance-root variable (x-instance-url-env / base_url_env with a fixed API path suffix) so per-instance connectors get this read generated.

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so a client cannot hold the listener open by dribbling request headers (gosec G112)
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.5 emits the streamable-HTTP http.Server in cmd/<slug>-mcp/main.go without a ReadHeaderTimeout; the repo security gate flags it as gosec G112 (P1) and datagate carries the identical hand-fix. The listener is the remote/hosted deployment path, so the deadline is a real hardening rather than a scanner appeasement.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press: set ReadHeaderTimeout in the generated MCP HTTP server template.

handfixes.summary: Zammad's MCP filesystem gate on top of the press's per-command blocked set: any flag whose usage text names a file or directory is refused at request time and removed from the tool schema (filesystem_gate.go isFilesystemPathFlag / UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags, typemap.go), and the connector's own path-taking names (from-csv, reconcile, a command-local home) are in blockedDestinationFlags.
handfixes.why: The press 4.34.0 gate blocks a fixed list of flag names; a novel command whose path flag has another name would still let an MCP argument choose a host file. The usage-text rule closes that for every present and future flag; the tree test walks every shell-out tool.

handfixes.summary: Every novel command declares where it reads from: the seven store-only analytics commands declare local and refuse --data-source live; the four API commands (kb browse, kb get, kb search, ticket note) declare live. The load, stale and orphans workflows are local-only too.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 dogfood hard-fails a novel without a data-source declaration, and before this agent-load --data-source live silently answered from the local store.

handfixes.summary: Local analytics refuse to answer from a partial store: novelRequireSynced gates every local command on a complete sync checkpoint, articles sync marks its checkpoint complete only on an unbounded full pass, and a ticket's stored articles are reconciled against the live list on refresh (removed articles are deleted; a null list is not read as empty).
handfixes.why: Codex review of the 4.34.0 reprint: articles sync --limit N marked the checkpoint complete, so local analytics could run on a partial article set, and removed articles stayed in the store.

handfixes.summary: No mirrored MCP tool sends a write to Zammad without a confirm step: ticket note is mcp:hidden (agents add a note through zammad_execute, which previews until confirm is true), and a tree test fails the build when a mirrored tool that is not read-only is missing from the allowlist of local-only tools. The two vendor writes the mirror does expose, webhooks_register and webhooks_unregister, are on a separate list the same test holds to a confirm argument: without confirm: true they print the plan and write nothing.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 publish: MCP ticket_note posted an article immediately, with no confirm.

handfixes.summary: Zammad webhooks instead of polling: `webhooks register|unregister|status` (webhooks.go), the `webhooks listen` receiver (webhooks_listen.go, HMAC-SHA1 check alone in webhook_signature.go), `events list` over a vendor_events table (store/vendor_events.go, created from extras.go), the signature secret beside the credentials file (cliutil/webhook_secret.go), held at startup with ZAMMAD_WEBHOOK_SECRET (credential_sources.go), and a streaming checked stderr line for the long-running listener (stderr_funnel.go stderrNow). Wired by novel_wiring.go. register, unregister and status act only on what register created (its webhook note, and triggers that fire those webhooks), never on an admin's own objects sharing the name prefix. Next-batch round 1: every vendor_events row passes the held check whole at the one insert (webhookListener.record); listen refuses to run while ZAMMAD_NO_LOCAL_DATA=1; ownership requires exactly the names register gives.
handfixes.why: Damien GO 2026-10-27: Zammad ships webhooks with its security reprint (fleet/state/plan-2026-10-27/webhooks.md sections 2 and 4). None of it is in the spec, so a reprint regenerates none of it: every file is hand-written with no DO NOT EDIT marker, and the three edits to generated files (extras.go migrations, novel_wiring.go hook, stderr_funnel.go stderrNow) plus the holder additions are pinned here. The listener verifies before parsing, drops replays by X-Zammad-Delivery and by event id, fetches the record instead of trusting the payload, and refuses to start without a secret or off loopback without TLS; proved against a local Docker Zammad 7.2.2 in .review/webhooks-e2e.md.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name, and no file stores operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds; ported by hand from the zammad output of tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py (that tool did not merge). The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. cliutil.RefuseHeld compares each operator-named write with every credential the secret funnel holds, whatever its length (FunnelHeldText), in every view it decodes, and refuses a match before it is written: profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl and the learn tables (learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home. Since the credential kit: the kit's file and SQLite sinks check each whole record as it is written, so the journal, teach log, audit, profile, feedback and learn-store checks of their own are gone; the session hash and the argv shape stay.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; restore each site these asserts pin (the apply tool did not merge).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

Yes, in the **ChatGPT desktop app**.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit is wired by hand: internal/cli/credkit_wiring.go carries the one credkit.Declarations literal, credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them, and every sink (stdout/stderr, files, SQLite through internal/kitsql, MCP, HTTP transport, child processes) passes the kit.
handfixes.why: Each per-connector credential check closed one shape and the next review found the next shape (a query value or userinfo in base_url, an 8-character piece of a token, a record checked before its last field was set). The kit holds every part of every credential at startup and checks every sink, so the shape stops mattering. A reprint rewrites the generated sinks and mains: these asserts make that fail instead of silently dropping the routing. The connector's own 0600 credential store and config rewrites are credential sources and stay outside the kit by contract.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.
tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #5041 (4.33.6): trustees are resolved to SIDs (LA through the OS) and compared by SID; the press generates the alias tests.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #5041 (4.33.6): the DACL section's flags and ACE list are framed (daclFlagsRe, aceListRe), so a NULL DACL behind flags is refused.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.
